ImageDescription.value: On the occasion of the 75th anniversary of the Basic Law, the Federal Republic of Germany organised a ‘Constitution Festival’. This took place mainly on Willy-Brand-Platz between the Chancellery and the Pual-Löbe-Haus, where the offices of the members of the Bundestag and the meeting rooms of the Bundestag committees are located, and on Platz der Republik between the Reichstag building on one side and the ‘Tipi’ and the ‘Haus der Kulturen der Welt’ on the other. In addition to the entertainment programme on stages on Willy-Brandt-Platz and Platz der Republik, information stands of various institutions were an important part of the event. NGOs were located on the meadow next to the Swiss Embassy. Federal ministries and federal authorities (such as the Federal Statistical Office and the Federal Office against Discrimination) had information stands along Paul-Löbe-Allee, which runs between the Reichstag, Paul-Löbe-Haus and the Chancellery from the Spree to the House of World Cultures. These stands of all federal ministries were supplied with internet via fibre optics. A fibre optic distribution box had previously been erected on the edge of Platz der Republik for this purpose. Since the end of the Constitution Festival, it has no longer been used and has been forgotten.  The optical fibres emanating from the box are exposed to the weather without protection. Their position is constantly changing due to external influences. There are unobstructed lines of sight between the distribution box and the Paul Löbe House, the Reichstag and the Chancellery. As the distribution box is located diagonally opposite one of the two entrances to the Chancellery and on the road used by city tours in double-decker buses, diplomats, media representatives, members of the legislative and executive branches of government, the Bundeswehr buses used by the state band to perform in the Chancellery during state visits by heads of government from other countries, it is seen every day by a large number of high-ranking politicians, civil servants, diplomats, press representatives and tourists from Berlin, the rest of Germany and the rest of the world. The photos with the name prefix ‘Bundesglasfaser’ document the changes over time to the distribution box and the fibre ends connected to it, starting with its construction in 2024 until the time when the box will either be dismantled again or the fibre ends will no longer be exposed to the weather in an untidy state. In view of its position in the middle of Germany's federal politics, this distribution box is ideally suited to illustrate and symbolise the devastating situation of digital policy in Germany. Bianca Kastl has coined the term ‘degitalisation’ to describe this regrettable digital policy.

Permission.value:
Until 31 December 2022, Article 25.1(h) of Law No. 50/2005/QH11 of November 29, 2005 amended by Law No. 36/2009/QH12 of June 19, 2009 provided a freedom of panorama provision for Vietnam, allowing photographs and television broadcasts of plastic arts, architecture, photographic works, and applied arts displayed in public spaces to be distributed to present images of these works.

This legal right did not cover other works like murals and literary texts on plaques or tables, as well as other types of representation of the covered works (like videos or films).

  • Intellectual Property Law of Vietnam of November 2005 (click "Tiếng Anh" for English); entry in force July 1, 2006.
  • Civil Code of Vietnam of September 2005 (click "Tiếng Anh" for English); contains in part 6 (articles 736 to 757) some additional copyright provisions (not relevant for freedom of panorama). In case of discrepancies between the Civil Code and the IP law, the IP law prevails (article 5 of the IP law).

This legal right did not cover other works like murals and literary texts on plaques or tables, as well as other types of representation of the covered works (like videos or films).
